correctness.rationale: The support functions give the directional-width maximum exactly. For a uniform direction, \(t=|b|\) is uniform on \([0,1]\); conditional angular symmetry converts the switching equation into \(\cos(2\phi)=r_\delta(t)\), with switching exactly for \(t<(1+\delta)^{-1}\). Differentiating the expectation gives the displayed first derivative. At the moving endpoint \(r_\delta=1\), boundary terms cancel; direct algebra yields the stated derivative and factorization for \(1-r_\delta^2\), giving the second derivative. Its numerator is positive on the integration region, the endpoint singularity is integrable, and dominated convergence gives the asymptotic slope \(\mathbb E|b|=1/2\).

value.rationale: Mean width is a standard intrinsic volume and this one-parameter family contains classical orthogonal-disk bodies studied only at special configurations. The exact sensitivity law and global convexity are structural information across the family.
residual_risks: Equal disks in perpendicular planes with displacement along the common line are assumed.
No closed form for every value \(W(\delta)\) is claimed.

final_claim: For the convex hull of two equal unit disks in perpendicular planes with center separation \(\delta\) along their common line, the directional width is \(A+B+\max\{|A-B|,\delta|b|\}\); the stated one-dimensional formulas for \(W'(\delta)\) and \(W''(\delta)>0\) hold for every \(\delta>0\), hence \(W\) is strictly convex and increasing, with \(W'(0+)=0\) and limiting slope \(1/2\).
scientific_limitations: Equal disks in perpendicular planes with displacement along the common line are assumed.
No closed form for every value \(W(\delta)\) is claimed.
